6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.SymPowColimit

9	/-!
10	# Naming the affine symmetric-power carrier: the quotient is `Spec` of the invariants
11	
12	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` reduced the symmetric-power obligation to one instance,
13	`HasColimit (permDiagram C n)`, and proved that the affine-algebra case is *inhabited*
14	at every `n`. But it flagged, three times and deliberately, that the resulting object
15	was **not identified**:
16	
17	> `mem_sections_singleObj_iff` is the *reason to expect* it … but it is a statement about
18	> `SingleObj G ⥤ Type` and mentions neither `CommRingCat` nor `Spec`. **The carrier is not
19	> named in Lean.**
20	
21	That gap is closed here. The colimit of a finite-group action on a ring, taken in
22	`CommRingCatᵒᵖ`, is `A^G` — the honest Milne `(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` once `A` is the `n`-fold
23	tensor power.
24	
25	## Why naming the carrier is real content, not bookkeeping
26	
27	The inhabitation statement `symPowData_affineAlgebra` comes from mathlib's colimits and
28	says only *some* object has the universal property. Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 says what
29	it **is**, and the difference is not cosmetic: the gluing step — the leg's remaining work
30	— has to compare the quotients of two overlapping charts. A comparison needs a formula for
31	each side. An abstract `colimit (permDiagram …)` supports no such comparison; `A^G` does,
32	because restriction of invariants along `A → A_b` is a ring map one can write down.
33	
34	So this file is the prerequisite for gluing, not a restatement of what was already known.
35	
36	## Main results
37	
38	* `actionDiagram G A` — the one-object diagram in `CommRingCat` of a `MulSemiringAction`.
39	  This is `permDiagram`'s algebraic counterpart: same index category `SingleObj G`.
40	* `fixedCone` / `fixedConeIsLimit` — **the identification, as a limit in `CommRingCat`**:
41	  the cone over `actionDiagram` with vertex the fixed subring `A^G` (mathlib's
42	  `FixedPoints.subring`) is a limit cone. Nothing is assumed about `G` — not even
43	  finiteness — because the universal property of the invariants needs none.
44	* `fixedCoconeIsColimitOp` — the same fact **dualised**: in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`, which is
45	  where the symmetric-power interface lives, `A^G` is a *colimit* of the action. This is
46	  the statement `SymPowColimit`'s §5 wanted and did not have.
47	* `hasColimit_actionDiagram_op` — hence the `HasColimit` instance for the opposite
48	  diagram, with the carrier now named.
49	
50	## Scope — read this before quoting it
51	
52	What is proved is the **affine, algebraic** identification: a limit in `CommRingCat` and
53	its dual in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`. Two things are deliberately *not* claimed:
54	
55	* This is not `Sym^n C` for a proper curve. The curve case is the gluing, and the gluing
56	  is not here. `SymPowColimit`'s §6 boundary sentence still stands verbatim: the affine
57	  universal property transfers into `Scheme` only against *affine* test objects.
58	* The index category here is `SingleObj G` for an arbitrary group acting on an arbitrary
59	  ring. Specialising `G := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` and `A := A^{⊗ n}` is what makes it Milne's
60	  statement; that specialisation needs the `S_n`-action on the tensor power, which mathlib
61	  has for modules and which is not built here.
62	
63	So: the carrier of the affine quotient is now a named object with a written-down universal
64	property, which is what the next step consumes. It is not the symmetric power of a curve.
65	
66	## References
67	
68	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.3 Proposition 3.1, p. 94. The consumer is
69	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §5; the interface is `Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean`.
70	-/
71

74	universe u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits
77	
78	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
79	
80	/-! ## §1. The action as a diagram in `CommRingCat`
81	
82	`permDiagram` (`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean`) bundles a group action as a functor out of
83	`SingleObj G`. The algebraic counterpart is the same construction with `End` taken in
84	`CommRingCat`, and the convention point is the mirror image of the one recorded there:
85	here the action is *covariant* on the ring, so no inverse is needed — a ring-level
86	`MulSemiringAction` composed with mathlib's `End` multiplication comes out right on the
87	nose (`mul_smul`). Contrast `permEnd`, which needs `σ⁻¹` because it acts on the
88	*geometric* side. -/
89	
90	/-- **A ring action, as a one-object diagram in `CommRingCat`.**
91	
92	The single value is `A` and the endomorphism at `g` is the ring automorphism `x ↦ g • x`.
93	A *limit* of this diagram is the invariant subring; dually, a colimit in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`
94	is the affine quotient. -/
95	noncomputable def actionDiagram (G : Type u) [Group G] (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
96	    [MulSemiringAction G A] : SingleObj G ⥤ CommRingCat.{u} :=
97	  SingleObj.functor (M := G) (X := CommRingCat.of A)
98	    { toFun := fun g => CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A g)
99	      map_one' := by apply CommRingCat.hom_ext; ext x; simp
100	      map_mul' := by
101	        intro g h
102	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
103	        ext x
104	        change (g * h) • x = g • h • x
105	        rw [mul_smul] }
106	
107	variable (G : Type u) [Group G] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [MulSemiringAction G A]
108	
109	@[simp]
110	theorem actionDiagram_obj (j : SingleObj G) :
111	    (actionDiagram G A).obj j = CommRingCat.of A := rfl
112	
113	/-- The diagram's map at `g` is the action of `g`, on elements. -/
114	theorem actionDiagram_map_apply (g : G) (x : A) :
115	    ((actionDiagram G A).map (SingleObj.toEnd G g)).hom x = g • x := rfl
116	
117	/-! ## §2. The invariants are the limit
118	
119	This is the identification. The cone is the inclusion `A^G ↪ A`, whose cone condition is
120	exactly "an invariant element is fixed by every `g`"; the limit property is the universal
121	property of a subtype — a cone vertex maps into `A` landing in the invariants, because the
122	cone condition *says* its image is fixed.
123	
124	Note what is **not** assumed: `G` is not finite, `A` is not Noetherian, and no integrality
125	enters. Finiteness is needed for the *geometry* of the quotient map (integrality,
126	surjectivity of `Spec A → Spec A^G`); the universal property itself is free. -/
127	
128	/-- **The cone over the action with vertex the invariant subring.** Its cone condition is
129	`x = g • x` for `x ∈ A^G`, i.e. the defining property of `FixedPoints.subring`. -/
130	noncomputable def fixedCone : Cone (actionDiagram G A) where
131	  pt := CommRingCat.of (FixedPoints.subring A G)
132	  π :=
133	    { app := fun _ => CommRingCat.ofHom (FixedPoints.subring A G).subtype
134	      naturality := by
135	        intro X Y f
136	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
137	        ext (x : FixedPoints.subring A G)
138	        change ((x : A)) = (f : G) • (x : A)
139	        exact (x.2 _).symm }
140	
141	@[simp]
142	theorem fixedCone_pt :
143	    (fixedCone G A).pt = CommRingCat.of (FixedPoints.subring A G) := rfl
144	
145	/-- **Milne's `(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}`, in the general form: the invariants ARE the limit.**
146	
147	The cone of `fixedCone` is a limit cone. Given any cone `c`, its leg at the unique object
148	lands in the invariants precisely by the cone condition `c.w`, so the lift is that leg
149	corestricted to `A^G`; uniqueness is injectivity of the inclusion.
150	
151	This is the declaration that names the carrier. `SymPowColimit`'s
152	`mem_sections_singleObj_iff` said a one-object diagram's *sections* are its fixed points,
153	about `SingleObj G ⥤ Type`; this says the *limit in `CommRingCat`* is the fixed
154	**subring**, which is the statement the quotient construction needs. -/
155	noncomputable def fixedConeIsLimit : IsLimit (fixedCone G A) where
156	  lift c := CommRingCat.ofHom
157	    { toFun := fun t => ⟨(c.π.app (SingleObj.star G)).hom t, by
158	        intro g
159	        have h := c.w (SingleObj.toEnd G g)
160	        exact congrArg (fun (f : c.pt ⟶ CommRingCat.of A) => f.hom t) h⟩
161	      map_one' := by ext; exact map_one _
162	      map_mul' := by intro x y; ext; exact map_mul _ _ _
163	      map_zero' := by ext; exact map_zero _
164	      map_add' := by intro x y; ext; exact map_add _ _ _ }
165	  fac c j := by
166	    obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star G := Subsingleton.elim _ _
167	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
168	    ext t
169	    rfl
170	  uniq c m hm := by
171	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
172	    ext t
173	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
174	    have h := hm (SingleObj.star G)
175	    exact congrArg (fun (f : c.pt ⟶ CommRingCat.of A) => f.hom t) h
176	
177	/-- **The invariant subring, as a limit — the `HasLimit` form.** -/
178	theorem hasLimit_actionDiagram : HasLimit (actionDiagram G A) :=
179	  ⟨⟨⟨fixedCone G A, fixedConeIsLimit G A⟩⟩⟩
180	
181	/-! ## §3. Dualised: the affine quotient is a colimit in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`
182	
183	The symmetric-power interface lives on the geometric side, so what it consumes is a
184	*colimit*. `IsLimit.op` crosses that gap with no further mathematics: a limit cone in
185	`CommRingCat` is a colimit cocone in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ` over the opposite diagram.
186	
187	This is the form `SymPowColimit`'s §5 wanted. Its `symPowData_affineAlgebra` produced the
188	interface from mathlib's colimits without knowing what the object was; the two together now
189	say the affine symmetric power exists **and** is `Spec` of the invariants. -/
190	
191	/-- **The affine quotient, named, as a colimit in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ`.**
192	
193	Dual to `fixedConeIsLimit`. The cocone vertex is `A^G` viewed in the opposite category —
194	geometrically, `Spec (A^G)` — and it is a colimit of the opposite action diagram.
195	
196	Read this as the algebraic half of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 *with its object
197	identified*: the quotient of `Spec A` by `G` is `Spec (A^G)`. The half that remains is
198	gluing such charts, for which see `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6. -/
199	noncomputable def fixedCoconeIsColimitOp :
200	    IsColimit (fixedCone G A).op :=
201	  (fixedConeIsLimit G A).op
202	
203	/-- **The `HasColimit` form of the affine quotient.** The obligation
204	`SymPowColimit.lean` isolates — a `HasColimit` for the action diagram — holds on the
205	opposite of `CommRingCat`, with the colimit now a named object rather than an abstract
206	one. -/
207	theorem hasColimit_actionDiagram_op : HasColimit (actionDiagram G A).op :=
208	  ⟨⟨⟨(fixedCone G A).op, fixedCoconeIsColimitOp G A⟩⟩⟩
209	
210	/-! ## §4. What this does and does not settle
211	
212	**Settled.** The affine symmetric-power carrier has a name and a proved universal property,
213	in both variances. Anyone building the gluing now has a formula for each chart's quotient
214	instead of an abstract colimit, which is what a chart-overlap comparison requires.
215	
216	**Not settled, and neither is smaller than it was.**
217	
218	* The curve case. `Over (Spec k̄)` with `C` proper still has no
219	  `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`, and this file does not touch it. What changed is the
220	  *input* to that construction, not the construction.
221	* The specialisation to Milne's actual ring. `G := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` acting on the
222	  `n`-fold tensor power `A^{⊗ n}` is the case Milne uses; the `S_n`-action on a tensor
223	  power of a commutative *ring* is not built here (mathlib's `SymmetricPower` /
224	  `TensorPower` symmetric API is for modules). So `A^G` above is Milne's
225	  `(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` only once that action is supplied.
226	
227	The second point is worth stating plainly because the header could be read as claiming
228	Milne's affine half outright. It does not: what is proved is the *general* invariants
229	identification, which is strictly more than the previous inhabitation statement and
230	strictly less than Milne III.3.1's affine case. -/
231	
232	end AlgebraicGeometry

2	name: project-git
3	description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
4	---
5	
6	Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.
7	
8	## The model
9	
10	- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
11	  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
12	  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
13	  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
14	  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
15	  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
16	  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
17	- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
18	  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
19	  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
20	- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
21	  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
22	  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
23	  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.
24	
25	So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
26	Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).
27	
28	## Recording your work (committing)
29	
30	Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
31	`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
32	would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:
33	
34	```bash
35	# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
36	"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
37	"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
38	  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
39	
40	# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
41	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
42	    add path/to/File.lean
43	git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
44	    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
45	    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
46	```
47	
48	Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
49	files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
50	anything staged in your way.
51	
52	- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
53	  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
54	  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
55	  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
56	  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
57	- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
58	  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
59	  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
60	  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
61	  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
62	  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
63	- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
64	  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
65	- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
66	  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
67	- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
68	  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
69	  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
70	- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
71	  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
72	  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
73	  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
74	  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
75	  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.
76	
77	Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
78	`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
79	make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:
80	
81	```bash
82	"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
83	```
84	
85	## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard
86	
87	Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
88	seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
89	then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
90	plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
91	The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
92	you did not ask for:
93	
94	- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
95	  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
96	  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
97	  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:
98	
99	  ```bash
100	  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
101	  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
102	  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
103	  ```
104	
105	- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
106	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.
107	
108	At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
109	since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
110	blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):
111	
112	```bash
113	"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
114	"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
115	```
116	
117	If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
118	working tree, commit once.
119	
120	## Reading history / a project's diff
121	
122	Run from the workspace root:
123	
124	```bash
125	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
126	
127	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
128	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
129	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
130	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
131	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
132	```
133	
134	Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
135	`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
136	run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:
137	
138	```bash
139	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
140	  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
141	```
142	
143	To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
144	the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
145	commit changed).
146	
147	## Caveats
148	
149	- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
150	  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
151	  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
152	  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
153	- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

23	tensor power.

25	## Why naming the carrier is real content, not bookkeeping
26	
27	The inhabitation statement `symPowData_affineAlgebra` comes from mathlib's colimits and
28	says only *some* object has the universal property. Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 says what

31	each side. An abstract `colimit (permDiagram …)` supports no such comparison; `A^G` does,
32	because restriction of invariants along `A → A_b` is a ring map one can write down.

41	  the cone over `actionDiagram` with vertex the fixed subring `A^G` (mathlib's

43	  finiteness — because the universal property of the invariants needs none.

99	      map_one' := by apply CommRingCat.hom_ext; ext x; simp
100	      map_mul' := by
101	        intro g h
102	        apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
103	        ext x
104	        change (g * h) • x = g • h • x
105	        rw [mul_smul] }

118	
119	This is the identification. The cone is the inclusion `A^G ↪ A`, whose cone condition is

168	    ext t

171	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
172	    ext t
173	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
174	    have h := hm (SingleObj.star G)
175	    exact congrArg (fun (f : c.pt ⟶ CommRingCat.of A) => f.hom t) h
176

178	theorem hasLimit_actionDiagram : HasLimit (actionDiagram G A) :=
179	  ⟨⟨⟨fixedCone G A, fixedConeIsLimit G A⟩⟩⟩
180

182	
183	The symmetric-power interface lives on the geometric side, so what it consumes is a
184	*colimit*. `IsLimit.op` crosses that gap with no further mathematics: a limit cone in
185	`CommRingCat` is a colimit cocone in `CommRingCatᵒᵖ` over the opposite diagram.
186

188	interface from mathlib's colimits without knowing what the object was; the two together now
189	say the affine symmetric power exists **and** is `Spec` of the invariants. -/
190

192	
193	Dual to `fixedConeIsLimit`. The cocone vertex is `A^G` viewed in the opposite category —
194	geometrically, `Spec (A^G)` — and it is a colimit of the opposite action diagram.
195	
196	Read this as the algebraic half of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 *with its object
197	identified*: the quotient of `Spec A` by `G` is `Spec (A^G)`. The half that remains is
198	gluing such charts, for which see `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6. -/
199	noncomputable def fixedCoconeIsColimitOp :
200	    IsColimit (fixedCone G A).op :=
201	  (fixedConeIsLimit G A).op
202	
203	/-- **The `HasColimit` form of the affine quotient.** The obligation
204	`SymPowColimit.lean` isolates — a `HasColimit` for the action diagram — holds on the
205	opposite of `CommRingCat`, with the colimit now a named object rather than an abstract
206	one. -/
207	theorem hasColimit_actionDiagram_op : HasColimit (actionDiagram G A).op :=
208	  ⟨⟨⟨(fixedCone G A).op, fixedCoconeIsColimitOp G A⟩⟩⟩

211	
212	**Settled.** The affine symmetric-power carrier has a name and a proved universal property,
213	in both variances. Anyone building the gluing now has a formula for each chart's quotient
214	instead of an abstract colimit, which is what a chart-overlap comparison requires.
215	
216	**Not settled, and neither is smaller than it was.**
217	
218	* The curve case. `Over (Spec k̄)` with `C` proper still has no
219	  `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)`, and this file does not touch it. What changed is the
220	  *input* to that construction, not the construction.
221	* The specialisation to Milne's actual ring. `G := Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` acting on the
222	  `n`-fold tensor power `A^{⊗ n}` is the case Milne uses; the `S_n`-action on a tensor
223	  power of a commutative *ring* is not built here (mathlib's `SymmetricPower` /
224	  `TensorPower` symmetric API is for modules). So `A^G` above is Milne's
225	  `(A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` only once that action is supplied.
226	
227	The second point is worth stating plainly because the header could be read as claiming
228	Milne's affine half outright. It does not: what is proved is the *general* invariants
229	identification, which is strictly more than the previous inhabitation statement and
230	strictly less than Milne III.3.1's affine case. -/

9	/-!
10	# Invariants commute with localization at an invariant element
11	
12	`Albanese/SymPowInvariants.lean` names the affine symmetric-power carrier: the quotient of
13	`Spec A` by a group action is `Spec (A^G)`. The next step of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 —
14	the gluing — needs to compare that quotient on two overlapping charts, and the overlaps of
15	an affine cover are localizations. So the comparison one needs is
16	
17	`(A_b)^G = (A^G)_b`  for `b` an invariant element,
18	
19	which mathlib does **not** have at this pin (measured: no lemma anywhere combines
20	`FixedPoints` / `Algebra.IsInvariant` with `Localization` in a commuting statement). This
21	file proves the substantive direction.
22	
23	## Why there is no averaging argument here
24	
25	Over a field of characteristic zero one divides by `|G|` and averages. That is unavailable:
26	the curve is over an arbitrary `k̄`, so `|G| = g!` may well be zero in `A`. The proof below
27	is characteristic-free and is the standard clearing argument:
28	
29	an invariant `x ∈ A_b` is *some* fraction `a / b^n`; invariance says `g • a` and `a` have the
30	same image in `A_b` for each `g`, so some power of `b` kills their difference. `G` is finite,
31	so one power `b^m` works for all `g` at once. Then `b^m · a` is **honestly invariant** in `A`
32	— using that `b` itself is invariant — and `x = (b^m a) / b^{m+n}` exhibits `x` as a fraction
33	with invariant numerator.
34	
35	Note where each hypothesis is spent: finiteness of `G` only takes a maximum over `G` of
36	finitely many exponents, and invariance of `b` is what makes `b^m · a` invariant rather than
37	merely `b^m`-torsion-equivalent to something invariant. Neither is decorative.
38

40	
41	* `powers_le_comap` — an invariant `b` has `g`-stable powers, the side condition
42	  `IsLocalization.map` consumes.
43	* `awayMap` — the induced action of `g` on `A_b`, with `awayMap_algebraMap` saying it is the
44	  action of `g` on numerators. This is the `G`-action on a chart overlap.
45	* `exists_invariant_numerator` — **the theorem**: an element of `A_b` fixed by every
46	  `awayMap` is a fraction whose numerator can be chosen invariant. This is the substantive
47	  half of `(A_b)^G = (A^G)_b`.
48	
49	## What is deliberately not claimed
50	
51	The converse inclusion — a fraction with invariant numerator is `awayMap`-fixed — is the
52	easy direction and is *not* proved here; nothing downstream needed it yet, and I would
53	rather leave it named than ship it unproved. So this file does **not** assert the equality
54	`(A_b)^G = (A^G)_b` as a ring isomorphism; it asserts the direction that a gluing argument
55	consumes (getting an invariant representative), which is the hard one.
56	
57	Nor is this the gluing. It is one input to it: the comparison map on a single overlap. The
58	cocycle condition across three charts is untouched.

78	/-- **An invariant element has `g`-stable powers.** The side condition
79	`IsLocalization.map` needs in order to push `g` through the localization at `b`. -/
80	theorem powers_le_comap (b : A) (hb : ∀ g : G, g • b = b) (g : G) :
81	    Submonoid.powers b ≤
82	      Submonoid.comap (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A g) (Submonoid.powers b) := by
83	  intro x hx
84	  obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := hx
85	  refine ⟨n, ?_⟩
86	  change b ^ n = g • (b ^ n)
87	  rw [smul_pow', hb g]
88	
89	/-- **The induced action on the chart overlap `A_b`.** For `b` invariant, `g` acts on the
90	localization `A_b` by acting on numerators. Geometrically this is the action of `G` on a
91	basic open subset of `Spec A` cut out by an invariant function — i.e. on the overlap of two
92	charts of a `G`-stable affine cover. -/
93	noncomputable def awayMap (b : A) (hb : ∀ g : G, g • b = b) (g : G) :
94	    Localization.Away b →+* Localization.Away b :=
95	  IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers b) (T := Submonoid.powers b)
96	    (Localization.Away b) (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A g) (powers_le_comap b hb g)
97	
98	/-- `awayMap` acts on numerators: it is the localization of the action. -/
99	@[simp]
100	theorem awayMap_algebraMap (b : A) (hb : ∀ g : G, g • b = b) (g : G) (a : A) :
101	    awayMap b hb g (algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) a)
102	      = algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) (g • a) :=
103	  IsLocalization.map_eq (powers_le_comap b hb g) a
104	
105	/-! ## §2. Clearing denominators to reach an invariant numerator
106	
107	The two steps of the characteristic-free argument, separated so each is checkable on its
108	own: first that a single `g` can be cleared, then that finitely many can be cleared
109	*simultaneously*. -/
110	
111	/-- **One `g` can be cleared.** If `g • a` and `a` agree in `A_b` then some power of `b`
112	equalises them already in `A`. This is `IsLocalization.exists_of_eq` with the annihilator
113	recognised as a power of `b`. -/
114	theorem exists_pow_smul_eq (b a : A) (g : G)
115	    (h : algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) (g • a)
116	      = algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) a) :
117	    ∃ m : ℕ, b ^ m * (g • a) = b ^ m * a := by
118	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := IsLocalization.exists_of_eq (M := Submonoid.powers b) h
119	  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := c.2
120	  refine ⟨m, ?_⟩
121	  have hbc : (b ^ m : A) = (c : A) := hm
122	  rw [hbc]
123	  exact hc
124	
125	/-- **All of `G` can be cleared at once.** Finiteness of `G` enters here and only here:
126	take the supremum of the finitely many exponents. -/
127	theorem exists_uniform_pow_smul_eq [Finite G] (b a : A)
128	    (h : ∀ g : G, ∃ m : ℕ, b ^ m * (g • a) = b ^ m * a) :
129	    ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ g : G, b ^ m * (g • a) = b ^ m * a := by
130	  classical
131	  cases nonempty_fintype G
132	  choose m hm using h
133	  refine ⟨Finset.univ.sup m, fun g => ?_⟩
134	  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ : ∃ k, Finset.univ.sup m = m g + k :=
135	    ⟨Finset.univ.sup m - m g, by
136	      have hle : m g ≤ Finset.univ.sup m := Finset.le_sup (Finset.mem_univ g)
137	      omega⟩
138	  rw [hk, pow_add]
139	  calc b ^ m g * b ^ k * (g • a)
140	      = b ^ k * (b ^ m g * (g • a)) := by ring
141	    _ = b ^ k * (b ^ m g * a) := by rw [hm g]
142	    _ = b ^ m g * b ^ k * a := by ring
143	
144	/-- **`b^m · a` is invariant.** The step that uses invariance of `b`: once one power of `b`
145	equalises `g • a` and `a` for every `g`, the *element* `b^m · a` is fixed by `G`.
146	
147	Without `hb` this would fail — `g • (b^m a) = (g • b)^m (g • a)`, and the first factor has
148	to come back. -/
149	theorem smul_pow_mul_eq (b a : A) (m : ℕ) (hb : ∀ g : G, g • b = b)
150	    (h : ∀ g : G, b ^ m * (g • a) = b ^ m * a) (g : G) :
151	    g • (b ^ m * a) = b ^ m * a := by
152	  rw [smul_mul', smul_pow', hb g, h g]
153	
154	/-! ## §3. The theorem -/
155	
156	/-- **The substantive half of `(A_b)^G = (A^G)_b`.**
157	
158	An element `x` of the localization `A_b` fixed by the induced action of every `g` is a
159	fraction whose numerator may be chosen **invariant**: there are `a ∈ A` invariant and `n`
160	with `x · b^n = a` in `A_b`.
161	
162	Characteristic-free — no averaging over `G`, which is unavailable since `|G|` may vanish in
163	`A`. The route is §2: pick any representative, clear each `g` (`exists_pow_smul_eq`), clear
164	all of them together (`exists_uniform_pow_smul_eq`, the only use of finiteness), then
165	`smul_pow_mul_eq` upgrades the cleared numerator to an honestly invariant element.
166	
167	This is the comparison a gluing argument consumes on a chart overlap: an invariant section
168	over the overlap comes from an invariant section upstairs, after shrinking by a power of the
169	invariant function cutting the overlap out. -/
170	theorem exists_invariant_numerator [Finite G] (b : A) (hb : ∀ g : G, g • b = b)
171	    (x : Localization.Away b) (hx : ∀ g : G, awayMap b hb g x = x) :
172	    ∃ (a : A) (n : ℕ), (∀ g : G, g • a = a) ∧
173	      x * algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) (b ^ n)
174	        = algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) a := by
175	  classical
176	  obtain ⟨⟨a, d⟩, hxa⟩ := IsLocalization.surj (Submonoid.powers b) x
177	  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := d.2
178	  have hd : (d : A) = b ^ n := hn.symm
179	  -- Invariance of `x` moves to its numerator, as an equation in `A_b`.
180	  have key : ∀ g : G, algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) (g • a)
181	      = algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) a := by
182	    intro g
183	    have h1 := congrArg (awayMap b hb g) hxa
184	    rw [map_mul, hx g, awayMap_algebraMap, awayMap_algebraMap] at h1
185	    rw [hd, smul_pow', hb g, ← hd] at h1
186	    rw [← h1, hxa]
187	  -- Clear denominators uniformly, then read off the invariant numerator.
188	  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ :=
189	    exists_uniform_pow_smul_eq b a (fun g => exists_pow_smul_eq b a g (key g))
190	  refine ⟨b ^ m * a, m + n, smul_pow_mul_eq b a m hb hm, ?_⟩
191	  rw [pow_add, map_mul, map_mul, ← mul_assoc, mul_comm (algebraMap A (Localization.Away b)
192	    (b ^ m)) (algebraMap A (Localization.Away b) (b ^ n))]
193	  rw [← mul_assoc, ← hd, hxa]
194	  ring
195	
196	end AlgebraicGeometry

23	## Why there is no averaging argument here
24	
25	Over a field of characteristic zero one divides by `|G|` and averages. That is unavailable:
26	the curve is over an arbitrary `k̄`, so `|G| = g!` may well be zero in `A`. The proof below

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.GrpObjFoldSum

/-!
# The symmetric power as an *interface*, and the two maps it produces

Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
Proposition 6.1) uses the `n`-th symmetric power `Sym^n C` only through its
**universal property**: every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors uniquely
through the symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`.

At this Mathlib pin the *object* `Sym^n C` does not exist for a proper curve — there is no
quotient of a scheme by a finite group action, and mathlib's `SymmetricPower` is for
modules. (The `analogies/m3-route-audit.md` figure of 2400–3800 lines priced Milne's
affine-and-glue route; `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` later reduced the obligation to one
`HasColimit` instance and discharged the affine half outright. Read that file before
budgeting anything from this paragraph.) Writing `Sym^n C := sorry` makes every downstream
equation a statement
about a junk term, which is why `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` keeps its obligations
unproved rather than discharging them against a meaningless definition.

This file takes the other route: it **names the interface** as a structure
`SymPowData C n`, and then proves, unconditionally, everything Milne's argument
derives from it. The missing geometry is isolated in exactly one place — inhabiting
`SymPowData` — and nothing downstream is a statement about `sorry`.

## What is proved here (no `sorry`, nothing conditional on unproved statements)

* `SymPowData.symAVMap` — Milne's `Sym^n φ`. Given `φ : C ⟶ A` into a *commutative*
  monoid object, the `n`-fold sum `powSum n φ` is `S_n`-symmetric
  (`MonObj.powSum_perm`, already proved), so the interface descends it. This is the
  content of `lem:symmetric_product_av_map`, and it is a construction, not a
  hypothesis.
* `SymPowData.proj_comp_symAVMap` / `SymPowData.symAVMap_unique` — its defining
  equation and uniqueness.
* `MonObj.basePointShift` — the morphism `Q ↦ (P₀, …, Q, …, P₀)` placing `Q` in a
  designated slot `i₀` and the basepoint elsewhere. Milne's `Q ↦ Q + (n−1) P₀`
  factors through it.
* `MonObj.basePointShift_comp_powSum` — **the computation that makes the backward
  direction of the Albanese connector work**: for a *pointed* `φ` (`P₀ ≫ φ = η[A]`),

  `basePointShift P₀ i₀ ≫ powSum n φ = φ`,

  because `φ(Q) + φ(P₀) + ⋯ + φ(P₀) = φ(Q) + η + ⋯ + η = φ(Q)`. In the hom-monoid
  this is `Finset.prod_ite_eq`; the geometry evaporates exactly as it does in
  `GrpObjFoldSum.lean`.
* `symPowDataOne` and `symPowDataOne_proj_perm` — **an inhabitant of the interface
  *together with* the symmetry hypothesis**: `Sym^1 C = C`. See the warning below for
  why both halves are needed and what they do and do not show.

## What non-vacuity does and does not mean here — read this before citing it

`SymPowData C n` **on its own is trivially inhabited for every `n`** — and the witness
is recorded below as `symPowDataTrivial` rather than left as a remark, so that nobody
has to rediscover it:

```
carrier := C^n,  proj := 𝟙,  desc := fun h _ => ⟨h, Category.id_comp h, …⟩
```

With `proj = 𝟙` the universal property degenerates to `∃! u, 𝟙 ≫ u = h`. So the bare
structure is nearly free, and exhibiting *some* `SymPowData` proves nothing.

What the downstream theorems actually quantify over is the **pair**
`(D, hproj)`, where `hproj : ∀ σ, permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj` says the projection
is genuinely symmetric. The `proj := 𝟙` trick fails that whenever `permAut C σ ≠ 𝟙`, which
for `n ≥ 2` holds as soon as `C` has two distinct global points — the case of interest, and
proved in `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` (`permAut_swap_ne_id_of_points`). It is *not*
automatic from `n ≥ 2` alone: at a **terminal** `C` the trivial datum does satisfy `hproj`
at every `n` (`permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal`), so an unqualified "fails for `n ≥ 2`" is
false. So the pair is the meaningful object away from that degenerate case, and this file
witnesses it for `n = 1`: `symPowDataOne` plus `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`.

Two honest caveats about that witness:

* `n = 1` is the case where the *interesting* step degenerates. The forward direction
  of the connector (`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`) uses that `ψ` is a homomorphism
  to move it through a `g`-fold product; a 1-fold product has one factor, so at
  `n = 1` that step is mere associativity. The general-`n` theorem is the real one —
  do not cite `n = 1` as evidence that the group law is exercised.
* Consequently, "the interface is inhabited" should be read as *the hypotheses are
  consistent and the statements are not about nothing*, not as *the hard case is
  covered*.

## What is *not* here — but see `Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` first

**This section is superseded in part (2026-07-28).** It said `SymPowData C n` for `n ≥ 2`
is "the missing quotient", the honest boundary of the leg. That reading was tied to one
presentation of the object — Milne's affine-and-glue construction — and
`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` replaces it:

* the pair `(D, hproj)` **is** a colimit of the `S_n`-action on `C^n`, in both directions
  (`symPowOfColimit`, `SymPowData.isColimit`, and `hasColimit_permDiagram_iff` for the
  equivalence, so the identification loses nothing);
* consequently `hproj` — the half that only `n = 1` witnessed here — is `colimit.w`, free
  at every `n`;
* and the **affine algebra** case is *inhabited* at every `n`
  (`symPowData_affineAlgebra`, in `(Under k)ᵒᵖ`), with no construction written. Note the
  careful wording: that is the inhabitation statement, not a formalisation of Milne III.3
  Proposition 3.1's affine half — identifying the carrier as `Spec (A^{⊗n})^{S_n}` is
  expected but **not proved**. See that file's §5 header.

What is genuinely still missing is the **gluing**, as `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` for the
curve at hand. So the boundary moved from a construction subproject to one instance about
one named diagram. (State it per-diagram, not as `HasColimitsOfShape … Scheme`: the
quantified form is strictly stronger and believed false at this pin.)

Also note the warning above is now *checked* rather than asserted: `permAut_swap_ne_id`
exhibits `permAut ≠ 𝟙` at a transposition (in `Type`, at `Bool`, `n = 2`), so
`symPowDataTrivial` demonstrably fails `hproj`. Nothing in this tree had verified that.

See `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` for the Albanese universal property proved over this
interface, `Albanese/AlbaneseFromColimit.lean` for the same statement with no `SymPowData`
argument at all, and the header of `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` for the pinned statements.

/-- **The universal property of the `n`-th symmetric power, as data.**

A `SymPowData C n` is a `carrier` (morally `Sym^n C`) together with a symmetrisation
morphism `proj : C^n ⟶ carrier` through which *every* `S_n`-symmetric morphism out of
`C^n` factors uniquely.

This is the interface, not the construction: see `symPowDataOne` for the case `n = 1`,
and the module header for why the general case is a separate subproject. -/

  carrier : K
  /-- The symmetrisation projection `π : C^n ⟶ Sym^n C`. -/
  proj : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ carrier
  /-- **The universal property.** Every `S_n`-symmetric morphism `C^n ⟶ T` factors
  uniquely through `proj`. -/
  desc : ∀ {T : K} (h : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ T),
    (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ h = h) →
    ∃! u : carrier ⟶ T, proj ≫ u = h

/-! ## §2. A colimit of the action is a `SymPowData`, with symmetry for free

This is the forward half of the identification. Note which part is doing the work: the
universal property of `SymPowData` is `colimit.desc` plus `colimit.hom_ext`, and the
symmetry hypothesis `hproj` — the half that ruled out the trivial witness and had only
an `n = 1` witness before — is `colimit.w`. Nothing is assumed about `n`. -/

section OfColimit

variable [HasColimit (permDiagram C n)]

/-- **The symmetric power from a colimit of the permutation action.**

`carrier := colimit (permDiagram C n)`, `proj := colimit.ι`, and the universal property is
`colimit.desc` — a symmetric `h` is a cocone by `symCocone`, and uniqueness is
`colimit.hom_ext` on the one-object index category. -/
noncomputable def symPowOfColimit : SymPowData C n where
  carrier := colimit (permDiagram C n)
  proj := colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _)
  desc := fun {T} h hsym => by
    have hd : colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _)
        ≫ colimit.desc (permDiagram C n) (symCocone C n h hsym) = h :=
      colimit.ι_desc (symCocone C n h hsym) (SingleObj.star _)
    refine ⟨colimit.desc (permDiagram C n) (symCocone C n h hsym), hd, ?_⟩
    intro u hu
    exact colimit.hom_ext fun j => by
      obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      exact hu.trans hd.symm

omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
@[simp]
theorem symPowOfColimit_carrier :
    (symPowOfColimit C n).carrier = colimit (permDiagram C n) := rfl

omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
@[simp]
theorem symPowOfColimit_proj :
    (symPowOfColimit C n).proj = colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _) := rfl

omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
/-- **The symmetry hypothesis, for free.** The projection of `symPowOfColimit` is
`S_n`-symmetric because that is the cocone condition `colimit.w`.

This is the declaration that changes the interface's status: `SymPowInterface.lean` needs
the *pair* `(D, hproj)`, and here `hproj` comes with the object at no cost and at every
`n`. -/
theorem symPowOfColimit_proj_perm (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ (symPowOfColimit C n).proj = (symPowOfColimit C n).proj := by
  have h := colimit.w (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.toEnd (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) σ⁻¹)
  change MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ colimit.ι (permDiagram C n) (SingleObj.star _) = _
  rw [permAut_eq_map C n σ]
  exact h

omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
/-- **The pair, packaged.** Existence of the object the Albanese theorems quantify over,
in the form a call site consumes: a `SymPowData` *together with* its symmetry. -/
theorem symPowData_of_hasColimit :
    ∃ D : SymPowData C n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj :=
  ⟨symPowOfColimit C n, symPowOfColimit_proj_perm C n⟩

end OfColimit

/-! ## §3. Conversely: the pair *is* a colimit

The other half of the identification, and the one that makes the reduction lossless. Any
`SymPowData` whose projection is symmetric exhibits its carrier as a colimit of
`permDiagram C n`.

Consequence worth stating explicitly, because it is what rules out having traded the
problem for a harder one: nobody can supply the pair `(D, hproj)` *without* supplying this
colimit. So `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` is not a sufficient condition that might be
stronger than needed — it is equivalent to the thing the Albanese argument consumes. -/

section ToColimit

/-- The cocone attached to a `SymPowData` with symmetric projection. -/
noncomputable def SymPowData.cocone (D : SymPowData C n)
    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj) :
    Cocone (permDiagram C n) where
  pt := D.carrier
  ι :=
    { app := fun _ => D.proj
      naturality := by
        intro X Y f
        change MonObj.permAut C (f : Equiv.Perm (Fin n))⁻¹ ≫ D.proj = D.proj ≫ 𝟙 _
        rw [Category.comp_id]
        exact hproj _ }

/-- **The pair is a colimit.** A `SymPowData` with symmetric projection is precisely a
colimit of the permutation action — its universal property *is* the colimit property,
transported across the fact that a cocone on a one-object diagram is a symmetric
morphism (`cocone_app_perm`). -/
noncomputable def SymPowData.isColimit (D : SymPowData C n)
    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj) :
    IsColimit (D.cocone C n hproj) where
  desc c := (D.desc (c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _)) (cocone_app_perm C n c)).choose
  fac c j := by
    obtain rfl : j = SingleObj.star _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    exact (D.desc (c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _)) (cocone_app_perm C n c)).choose_spec.1
  uniq c u hu :=
    (D.desc (c.ι.app (SingleObj.star _)) (cocone_app_perm C n c)).choose_spec.2 u
      (hu (SingleObj.star _))

omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
/-- **The obligation is exactly a `HasColimit`.** Supplying the pair the Albanese
theorems quantify over is equivalent to the diagram having a colimit — so replacing
"construct `Sym^n C`" by `HasColimit (permDiagram C n)` neither weakens nor strengthens
the problem. -/
theorem hasColimit_permDiagram_iff :
    HasColimit (permDiagram C n) ↔
      ∃ D : SymPowData C n, ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
        MonObj.permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj := by
